Case studies are also presented in this paper in order to depict the applications of the problem of inverse power flow in the power system engineering. Title: Selective publication in Nature : An empirical analysis of abstracts from the Journal of Statistical Genetics Abstract: In this paper, we are going to analyze the selective publication of manuscripts in the journal Nature. First we are going to analyze the frequency of abstracts in the manuscripts that are published in the journal Nature Genetics. Is there any difference in the frequency of abstracts between authors, issues or fields of specialization? We are going to detect the significant association, but there is no difference in frequency of abstracts with respect to the Journal number (JSS). Then we are going to analyze the selective publication in the journal Nature Genetics with respect to the geographical location and also the corresponding geographical Journal issues with respect to whether they are journals (SSJ) or journals at the top of field of specialization. We are going to detect the same result. New analysis and new hypotheses are proposed. First analysis of the selective publication : In this analysis we are going to compute the frequency of abstracts with respect to the author, issue and the field of specialization. In this analysis, we are going to use the logistic regression model to estimate the frequency of abstracts with respect to the author, the issue and the field of specialization. From the estimate we are going to propose two hypotheses. (i) Journals publish the manuscripts with same quality within the same field of specialization. (ii) Journals publish only those manuscripts which are not having any papers or manuscripts with small number of original articles. Second analysis of the selective publication : We are going to examine the manuscripts with respect to the author, issue and geographical location. We are going to detect that the frequency pattern of the abstracts and manuscripts are different for those manuscripts published in the top journals. The difference is going to be detected by taking into account the publication status and authorship by geographical location using a logistic regression analysis. This will be discussed in details in the 13th week of conference in October 2014.

Arie Lev Gruzman (born July 1, 1948) is an academic, scholar of Jewish studies. Arie Lev Gruzman is director of the Center for Jewish Studies at Georgetown University. Biography 
Arie Lev Gruzman was born in Tel Aviv, Israel on July 1, 1948. Lev Gruzman is a descendant of Holocaust survivors. He received a B.A. degree in Hebrew from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel, in 1969 and a degree in Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations from Harvard University, United States, in 1977. Lev Gruzman has taught at the University of Pennsylvania, the University of California, Berkeley, and Georgetown University since 1985. Lev Gruzman has served as director of the Center for Jewish Studies at Georgetown University since 1995. Research and interests

Arie Lev Gruzman has written many articles and books. Among these are Jews and the Dead Sea Scrolls (1992), and The Jewish Jesus: How Jewish Theology Influenced the New Testament (2000).
Arie Lev Gruzman has participated in interfaith initiatives.
Arie Lev Gruzman has consulted with the Vatican's Pontifical Council for Interreligious Dialogue.
Arie Lev Gruzman has been a member of the National Council of Churches' Committee on Faith and Order.
Arie Lev Gruzman has participated in Jewish-Muslim dialogues.
Arie Lev Gruzman has co-founded the Georgetown-Sultan Qabas University Dialogue Initiative, a joint initiative of Georgetown University and Sultan Qabas University, created to foster interfaith dialogue and interfaith learning among students and scholars of both universities.
Arie Lev Gruzman has been awarded the National Jewish Book Award in 2012, for his book The Jewish Jesus: How Jewish Theology Influenced the New Testament.

In this paper we have proposed an efficient technique to do the topological image segmentation based on the topological derivative and Automatic sign language recognition. Topological derivative of the video images taken from the video files was computed using the watershed transformation algorithm. Gradient magnitude was used to find the topological derivative of the video images. Video images and its isotropic filters was used to find the topological derivative of the video images. Isotropic filter and its applications with the watershed transformation algorithm to find the gradient magnitude of the video images have been discussed. Efficient and robustness of the proposed method for image segmentation using the watershed transformation algorithm was established. Classification of the image segmentation was done using the statistical features of the segmented image from the normalized RGB histogram. Feature selection technique was applied based on the Fisher score to reduce the dimensionality of the input space and find the features useful for recognition. At last the classifier used was the kNN classifier to recognize the gesture sequence. The proposed method was tested using the Texas Instruments DLP sign language gesture database and recognition rate was 95.6%.

Mr Lapid has already met with the head of the US central bank. The Israeli government has already met executives at JPMorgan Chase to discuss the position. Andy Haldane, chief economic adviser at the UK's Bank of England, is one of the candidates being considered for the post. The US-Israeli relationship has recently suffered from a cooling due to the Jewish state's settlements in the West Bank. Israel's prime minister Mr Bennett said his country has a "good relationship" with the US.

The Fife Coalfield was a coal mining area located in the modern Scottish administrative area of Fife. Most of the coal mines operated in the adjacent counties of Angus and Kinross. The first coal mine was opened in the area in 1575. Over 300 coal mines operated in the area, and the Fife Coalfield was one of the most productive areas of coal mining in the United Kingdom. The area was unimportant to the UK, as the UK switched from coal to oil at the end of the 19th century. The last coal mine in the area closed in 1966, ending coal mining in the area. The area is historically very important and there are numerous memorials and sites associated with the coal industry. There is a Scottish Mining Museum at Newtongrange in the area, which is a tourist attraction. There are also other sites of historical interest associated with the coal industry in this area.

We propose and analyze two new strategies to solve the segmentation problem of multiple organs in the deep learning context. The strategies are based on the use of the parallel input channels from the different planes with different supervisory strategy which can be used for solving the problem of ambiguity due to the presence of partial and irrelevant annotations in the semi-supervised strategies. We show how to extend the co-training supervisory strategy to different planes using a two-step strategy consisting of convolutional autoencoder and a 3D residual neural network. The proposed strategies are able to capture the complementarity of appearance and geometry representation from input images and are able to achieve significant improvement over the performance of unimodal input single planes and end-to-end deep learning strategies. We show that similar performance can be achieved by employing similar strategies on similar algorithms. The performance achieved on 5 public datasets containing brain tumour slices is the state of the art performance as compared to human experts without any interactive finetuning.

The following is an abstract for a research paper titled "CIDI-Lung-Seg: A single click annotation tool for automatic delineation of the lungs from CT scans"
Manual delineation of the lungs from CT scans is currently the standard-of-care procedure for the diagnosis of the lungs cancer. Manual delineation of the lungs from CT scans is a very tedious and time-consuming process and is also prone to errors. In this research paper, we are introducing a novel approach for the automatic delineation of the lungs from CT scans using a 'single click annotation tool'. CIDI-Lung-Seg is a tool that uses a pre-trained deep learning algorithm to perform automatic delineation of the lungs from CT scans. The proposed method is able to automatically identify the location of the lungs and generate a fully segmented image from CT scans using a 'single click annotation tool'. In a blinded and controlled study, we have demonstrated that the performance of CIDI-Lung-Seg is statistically significant compared to the performance of a manual annotation tool. We have demonstrated that the overall agreement is 96.2 percent and the Kappa value is 0.87 for manual annotation. We have also demonstrated that the time required for the annotation task has been reduced by 87.2 percent compared to the time required for the manual annotation task. Our proposed novel method for the automatic delineation of the lungs from CT scans will help to reduce the time and effort that is currently being spent on the manual delineation of the lungs from CT scans for the diagnosis and treatment of the lungs cancer. The proposed CIDI-Lung-Seg will be a very useful tool for the radiologists, oncologists and other medical professionals involved in the diagnosis and treatment of the lungs cancer.

Medical image segmentation is a key problem in clinical analysis and computer-aided diagnosis, especially for medical image segmentation with 3D medical images. Compared to 2D medical images, 3D medical images have more rich structures. But it is more challenging and robust to perform medical image segmentation. Even though 3D medical images contain more information, but it is very challenging to extract these information for medical image segmentation. In this paper, we aim to design a novel network architecture for 3D medical image segmentation. We design a novel network architecture for medical image segmentation, called UpSampled encoder-decoder (USNet) network architecture with multi-level feature aggregation. This novel USNet network architecture can be efficiently used to extract low-level features from 3D medical images for learning rich spatial features of USNet network architecture. Additionally, the USNet network architecture can be used to extract features of different levels from 3D medical images for learning complex structures. Furthermore, this network can be used to extract better features to achieve better image segmentation performance. We perform the comprehensive experiments on three representative benchmark datasets: ISLES2017 dataset, LLC dataset and the SYNAPSE-BREAST-CT dataset in this paper. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/CCF-Union/UXNet
